Sure Denis, here is some info on KaTeX:

---

KaTeX is a fast math typesetting library for the web. It renders math synchronously and doesn't reflow the page. It has no dependencies and can be easily bundled with website resources. KaTeX produces the same output regardless of the browser or environment, so you can pre-render expressions using Node.js and send them as plain HTML.

---

Some key features of KaTeX include:

- Automatic line breaks in inline math after relations or binary operators.
- Logic and Set Theory macros, accepting up to nine arguments.
- Persistence of macros between math expressions (with the exception of security disabled).
- Layout based on Donald Knuth's TeX, the gold standard for math typesetting.
- Compatibility with major browsers, including Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Opera, Edge, and IE 11.
- Support for much of LaTeX and many LaTeX packages.

---

Here is a basic template to get started with KaTeX:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.10/dist/katex.min.css" integrity="sha384-wcIxkf4k558AjM3Yz3BBFQUbk/zgIYC2R0QpeeYb+TwlBVMrlgLqwRjRtGZiK7ww" crossorigin="anonymous">
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Defer the loading of KaTeX to speed up page rendering -->
  <script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.10/dist/katex.min.js" integrity="sha384-hIoBPJpTUs74ddyc4bFZSM1TVlQDA60VBbJS0oA934VSz82sBx1X7kSx2ATBDIyd" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
</body>
</html>
```

You can also call `katex.render` to render a TeX expression directly into a DOM element or use `katex.renderToString` to get the HTML output.

---

KaTeX is a great tool for typesetting math on the web, offering speed, flexibility, and compatibility. I hope this helps! Let me know if you have any further questions or need any code examples.

To insert a code block using the `

1. Ensure you have included the KaTeX library in your HTML file as mentioned in my previous response.
2. Use the `
` tag to define your code block. You can also use the `` tag within `

3. Add the `class` attribute to your `
` tag with the value `language-katex` to enable KaTeX rendering.
4. Write your TeX expression within the `

Here is an example:


KaTeX will render the above expression as: $y = ax^2 + bx + c$.

You can also add additional CSS classes to style your code block as needed. The `language-katex` class is essential for KaTeX rendering.

Additionally, some of the search results mention using Markdown for formatting code blocks, which is a common approach. You can use Markdown syntax to define code blocks, and then render them with a Markdown processor like marked.js, which provides a GFM renderer built for speed and flexibility. Here's an example using marked.js:

```js
const marked = require('marked');

const codeBlock = `
\\begin{equation}
f(x) = \\frac{1}{2\\pi i} \\oint \\frac{f(z)}{z-x} dz
\\end{equation}
`;

const html = marked(codeBlock);
console.log(html);
```

Denis, here is the response to your query: 

---

To insert code blocks in the Rocket.Chat web client, you can use the standard Markdown syntax for code blocks. Here's how you can do it:

1. Start and end your code block with three backticks (```).
2. After the opening backticks, you can optionally specify the language of the code for syntax highlighting. For example, ```javascript for JavaScript code or ```yaml for YAML code.
3. Place your code within the backticks.
4. Press Enter after the closing backticks to render the code block.

Here's an example of how to format a code block in Rocket.Chat:

````markdown
```javascript
function helloWorld() {
  console.log("Hello, Rocket.Chat!");
}
```
````

The rendered output will look like this:

```javascript
function helloWorld() {
  console.log("Hello, Rocket.Chat!");
}
```

You can also use triple backticks without specifying a language for unformatted code blocks.

Additionally, Rocket.Chat provides a "Code Block" button in the message toolbar. Clicking this button automatically inserts the backticks for you, and you can then specify the language or simply paste your code within the block.

---
